name: Shein
summary: Shein is a Singapore-headquartered, China-founded online fast-fashion retailer built around a global, app-led supply chain.
overview: Shein sells low-cost fashion directly to consumers across a large number of markets. It listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange on September 1, 2026, establishing a public-market reference point for the business.

facts.label: IPO valuation
facts.note: As of Sept. 1, 2026. Reuters reported this valuation at Shein's Hong Kong IPO.

facts.label: 2025 net revenue
facts.note: As of the year ended Dec. 31, 2025. Disclosed in the Hong Kong listing materials.

facts.label: Public status
facts.note: As of Sept. 1, 2026. Listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange (stock code 0625).

bull_case: A highly efficient global direct-to-consumer platform can compound through scale, assortment, logistics, and new categories.
bear_case: Regulatory scrutiny, supply-chain allegations, import-rule changes, and a possible valuation reset could materially weaken the investment case.
latest_round: September 2026: Hong Kong IPO at a reported $26.5B valuation

intelligence.description: Shein operates a global online fashion marketplace with a supply chain centered in China and a consumer brand distributed primarily through its app and website.
company: Shein built its business by pairing social and app-led demand generation with a broad network of suppliers, enabling fast iteration across a very large catalogue of low-priced apparel and other consumer goods.

Shein raised $2 billion in May 2023 at a reported $66 billion private valuation. It then completed a Hong Kong IPO in September 2026, which Reuters reported valued the company at about $26.5 billion and raised about $1.7 billion. The IPO, rather than the 2023 financing, is now the most recent disclosed valuation event.
intelligence.why_it_matters: Shein is a large global e-commerce platform whose Hong Kong listing provides a public-market reference point after years of private-market valuation debate. Regulatory exposure, supply-chain scrutiny, and cross-border trade policy remain material to assessing the business.

changed.text: Reported valuation reaches roughly $100B during a period of rapid private-market growth.
A reported $2B financing marks the company at $66B.
Net revenue rose nearly 8% to $41.85B, according to the Hong Kong listing materials.
Shein completed its Hong Kong IPO and began trading on September 1; Reuters reported an IPO valuation of about $26.5B.

takeaways: The $26.5B IPO valuation is the most recent disclosed valuation reference; the $66B figure is a dated 2023 private-market mark.
Shein's supply-chain speed and global demand engine are its key operating advantages.
Labor, environmental, regulatory, and trade-policy risks are fundamental—not peripheral—to the story.
The completed IPO establishes a public-market reference point, but does not remove the underlying regulatory and trade-policy risks.

sources.label: Reuters: Hong Kong IPO debut and valuation
